name: xometry
description: Xometry CNC machining (a network of shops): general tolerance +/-0.005 in on metals, edges broken by default, anything tighter by drawing. Stands in for an equivalent online CNC bureau; every figure carries the page it was read on.
how_read: plain page fetches on 2026-11-15, no account, no upload, no quote. The CNC design guide is a PDF behind a contact form and was NOT read.
sigma_rule: a published +/- tolerance is taken as two standard deviations, the convention of mechloop/tolerance/process.py

notes: cast specifically for applications that require highly accurate components like assembly jigs, test structures, and fixture plates ... its crystal structure has no internal stresses

materials_not_listed.al_atp5: ATP-5 is not in the list; 'choose "Custom" under the material drop-down ... submit your quote for manual review'

al_mic6.note: RECALLED, not published by Xometry: MIC-6 is made in inch thicknesses (1/4, 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4, 1 in). SendCutSend's list (.250, .375, .500 in) agrees for the first three, and the maker's brochure held in mechloop/parts/vendor/cast_tooling_plate.json states flatness for '1/4 to 5/8 in' and '3/4 in and thicker' plate. An 8 mm cast plate is not MIC-6 stock.

general_tolerance_mm.verbatim: For features of size (Length, width, height, diameter) and location (position, concentricity, symmetry) +/- .005” (metals) or +/- .010 (plastics and composites) following ISO 2768 unless otherwise specified.

form_tolerance_mm.unit: mm over part length [up to mm, tolerance]
form_tolerance_mm.verbatim: Parallelism, Perpendicularity, Cylindricity, Circularity, Concentricity, Flatness, and Straightness over Part Length: 0 to 12" .005" 0.5° ; 12" to 24" .010" 0.5° ; 24" - 36" 1/64" (.016") 1° ; 36" - 60" 1/32" (.031") 1° ; Over 60" 1/16" (.063") 1°

tight_tolerance.verbatim: Xometry can manufacture and inspect to tight tolerances, including sub +/- 0.001" tolerances, per your drawing specifications and GD&T callouts.
tight_tolerance.note: needs a drawing; priced per quote

edge_break.verbatim: Sharp edges will be broken and deburred by default. Critical edges that must be left sharp should be noted and specified on a print.
edge_break.note: No radius or chamfer size is published. The 'Standard (As-Milled)' finish text on the CNC page reads differently: 'Machined parts are left with visible tool marks and potentially sharp edges and burrs, which can be removed upon request.' State the edge break on the drawing.

workmanship_edges.verbatim: All exposed edges will be free of burrs, sharp edges, and metal slivers.* *Parts made with Sheet Cutting are not deburred unless specified through a selected finish.

surface_finish.verbatim: As machined surface finish is 125 Ra or better. Machine tool marks may leave a swirl-like pattern.

min_feature_mm.verbatim: Minimum Feature Size | 0.020” (0.50 mm). This may vary depending on part geometry and chosen material.

max_part_milled_mm.verbatim: Milled parts up to 80” x 48” x 24” (2,032 x 1,219 x 610 mm). Lathe parts up to 62” (1,575 mm) length and 32” (813 mm) diameter.

max_part_by_axes_mm.verbatim: 5 Axis Machining up to 26″ ; 4 Axis Machining up to 36″ ; 3 Axis Machining up to 60″ (general guidelines; larger goes to quote review)

wall_min_metal_mm.verbatim: As a general rule of thumb, CNC machined walls should have a minimum width of 1/32” (0.794mm).

corner_depth_ratio.verbatim: use an inside corner radius that has a L:D ratio (length to diameter) of 3:1 or less

corner_radius_margin_mm.verbatim: we recommend modeling your design with at least 0.02″ – 0.05″ added to internal corner radii

thread_depth_ratio.verbatim: you don't need to thread a hole to more than 3X the hole's diameter (and keep it shorter, if possible)

thread_sizes.verbatim: Xometry can accommodate any standard thread size. We can also machine custom threads; these will require a manual quote review. ... Anything smaller than a 2-56 requires hand tapping

thread_callout.verbatim: Tapped holes not explicitly called out as Features on the quoted CAD model may be machined to the diameters specified in that model.

hole_depth.verbatim: NOT READ on a fetched page: the hole depth-to-diameter figure is in the gated design guide. mechloop's general rule (Hubs: 10 x typical) stays in force.

standard_sizes.verbatim: conventional fractions of an inch, like 1/8”, 1/4”, or whole numbers of millimeters will be “standard.” Avoid using measurements like 0.492” or 3.841 mm.

inspection_standard.verbatim: Standard Inspection: ... If no dimensional print is provided with a part, QC measures to Xometry's Manufacturing Standards on dimensions they deem critical, such as overall size, holes, and depths. If a dimensional print is provided, QC will verify up to 20 dimensions they deem critical. Documentation will not be shipped with your parts.

inspection_options.verbatim: Formal Inspection with Dimensional Report; CMM Inspection with Dimensional Report; First Article Inspection Report (FAIR AS9102); Source Inspection; Custom Inspection. A customer-supplied dimensional print is required for each.

finishes.verbatim: Standard (As-Milled); Bead Blast; Tumbled (parts over 8” may require a manual review); Anodized (Type II or Type III); Chem Film (provides corrosion resistance and good conductivity properties ... adds very little thickness, about 0.00001”-0.00004”); Powder Coat; Zinc Plating

no_finish_unless_ordered.verbatim: No surface treatments (e.g. anodize, bead blast, iridite, powder coat, etc.) will be applied unless you have paid for them and we have specifically acknowledged them.

large_part_flatness.verbatim: +.005”/-.005” local tolerances across most geometries in metals ... Will vary for large parts, specifically when holding flatness over large parts after heat treatment.

basis.pos: half of +/-0.127 mm (features of location, no drawing)
basis.hole_sd: half of +/-0.127 mm (features of size, no drawing)
basis.flat: half of .005 in (0.127 mm) form tolerance, part length 0 to 12 in
basis.pattern: class value kept: no figure for features cut in one set-up is published

basis.flat: half of .010 in (0.254 mm) form tolerance, part length 12 to 24 in
half of 1/64 in (0.406 mm), part length 24 to 36 in; longer parts are looser still

material_rules.text: a material not in the published list goes to manual quote review ('Custom')
cast tooling plate used for flatness must be a thickness the plate is made in, or both faces are machined and the stock's flatness is lost (thickness list recalled, not published)
every tapped hole must be called out as a thread feature in the quote or on a drawing
anything tighter than +/-0.127 mm, any flatness under 0.127 mm, any edge that must stay sharp or have a stated break: on a drawing

not_published: the size of the default edge break
stock plate thicknesses (the network sources material; MIC-6 thicknesses here are recalled)
hole depth-to-diameter, pocket depth and minimum hole diameter rules (in the gated design guide; mechloop's general rules stay in force)
which tolerance class of ISO 2768 (the page says 'in accordance with ISO 2768' beside +/-0.005 in; it names no class)
a positional tolerance between features cut in one set-up
